children.title: Implement explicit-target Schedule CLI operations
children.description:
Objective: expose the seven Schedule operator commands and Schedule Doctor presentation using existing typed SDK transports, with deterministic explicit input and no local host execution.

Target contract: schedule:add requires exactly one explicit --node=ID or --instance=ID with a positive integer ID. Both/neither, malformed/non-positive IDs, or target-inapplicable options fail before any HTTP. --no-start is AppInstance-only and sends start=false. Apply identical rules in interactive, non-interactive, and --json modes; do not add name lookup, discovery requests, or a target picker. schedule:list stays the existing unfiltered SDK operation; show/run/logs/remove/activate use the Schedule UUID. Completion remains internal Node-authenticated API/SDK transport; never expose schedule:complete.

Implementation boundary: apps/cli/app/Commands/Schedules/**, DoctorCommand, existing CLI registration/inventory/guidance, their focused CLI tests, CLI README, docs/reference/schedules.md and generated context when required. Reuse GatewayCommand, existing connector/error/rendering conventions, NodeScheduleTarget/AppInstanceScheduleTarget, and typed Schedule responses. SDK DoctorFamily already includes Schedule. Read the assigned worktree and nearest guidance. The retained docs-only candidate 6d9e9b294ea30d878366b3128e78edbedb3ad0ba is historical starting context, not a fixed future HEAD gate. Correct the prior ambiguous-target documentation. Do not restart the legacy plan/resolver loop or implement against an unapproved alternative contract.

Excluded: Gateway or SDK source changes, runtime provisioning, host SSH/systemd/journalctl/curl/shell execution by the operator commands, dependency upgrades, harness changes, live-fleet mutation, new ADRs, unrelated feature fixes, automatic merge. If acceptance exposes an out-of-scope defect, retain evidence and report the precise blocker for coordinator routing.

Verification: meaningful affected CLI Pest through composer test:affected with unfiltered TIA; CLI composer check; docs-lint for maintained docs. Keep caller Commander app/database/cache/provider environment out of project checks and use disposable project-local test configuration. A zero-selected run is not acceptance. After package approval and authorized admission, use the issue discovery topology for the two named Schedule acceptance observations. Await each topology command before the next and never bypass its lock. Acquisition readiness is not acceptance. Incus setup may use current supported product operations on disposable nodes; it must not add product deployment code or depend on finishing ORB-91 merely to obtain a topology.

Handoff: for each C1-C12, record exact command, cwd or topology/node, actual outcome and exit, retained log/reference, and temporary machine changes plus cleanup/remaining state. Submit through the assigned Commander receipt, then yield. The same implementer handles corrections; only the assigned reviewer commits after pass. The finished candidate gate and integrated review follow child acceptance under the root contract.

References: docs/reference/schedules.md; accepted ADRs docs/decisions/0004-verify-only-doctor-boundary.md, 0013-native-systemd-schedule-management.md, 0047-create-production-appinstances-from-candidates.md, 0048-copy-app-process-and-schedule-definitions-into-appinstances.md and 0060-record-latest-schedule-run-status.md. ADR0060 supersedes generation-based completion; no generation/run-history work is assigned. The existing transports are packages/php-sdk/src/Requests/Schedules/{AddScheduleRequest,ListSchedulesRequest,ShowScheduleRequest,RunScheduleRequest,ScheduleLogsRequest,RemoveScheduleRequest,ActivateScheduleRequest}.php and typed Responses/Schedules. For C12, observe stopped production installation before its first release, then use a supported explicit release to obtain the runtime directory; manual run after release must leave the timer disabled, and explicit repeated activation must preserve the same UUID. Production means a disposable app-prod target, never the live fleet. Existing SDK/Gateway tests are reference evidence, not a substitute for these actual CLI observations.

Current-main prerequisite alignment: before admission the coordinator integrates reviewed main 5635adccf37c904e8890577463b70c3704b760c3 into the retained branch without rewriting the authored documentation commit. This brings known test-safety, test-runner and discovery clone/schema repairs. Doctor's Schedule help support already exists (126dd1cc); retain it and prove C5 without duplicating implementation. 32a08b5c removed Laravel's unrelated local scheduler classes. Keep those classes removed in config/commands.php, and update UnknownCommandTest/CommandSurfaceTest as needed so schedule:list and schedule:run resolve only to the new HTTP-only Orbit adapters, not Illuminate's scheduler. schedule:finish and schedule:complete stay absent. This changes the operator surface under the existing ORB71 outcome, not the prohibition on local scheduling.
children.acceptance_criteria:
C1: Each of the seven operator commands sends exactly one SDK request for its operation and renders the typed response in human and `--json` form with the request ID, and a Gateway failure renders the shared safe error. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.

C2: `schedule:add` requires exactly one explicit `--node=ID` or `--instance=ID` with a positive integer ID. Both selectors, neither selector, a malformed or non-positive ID, or an option that belongs to the other target kind fails before any HTTP request. `--no-start` is AppInstance-only. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.

C3: `schedule:list` output contains no command text and `schedule:logs` renders only the bounded lines the Gateway returns. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.

C4: Interactive, non-interactive, and `--json` calls apply the same explicit-selector rules. Invalid target input returns a bounded error naming the required selector or invalid identity, never opens a target-selection prompt, and sends no discovery or operation request. `schedule:list` uses its existing unfiltered SDK operation; show, run, logs, remove, and activate identify one Schedule by UUID rather than by new target selectors. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.

C5: `orbit doctor --family=schedule` is accepted and renders the `schedule` family at its position in the ordered family set without asserting a numeric family count. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Doctor/DoctorCommandTest.php`.

C6: The command inventory and guidance list the seven operator commands, state that completion remains internal Node-authenticated API and SDK transport, and name no local host-execution dependency. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/BoostGuidanceTest.php`.

C7: From the operator machine, `schedule:add`, `schedule:show`, `schedule:run`, `schedule:logs`, and `schedule:remove` succeed against a real Node target and a real app-dev AppInstance target, and the logs output shows the run's journald lines. Proof: Incus action `schedule-cli-lifecycle`.

C8: Maintained documentation states the seven operator Schedule commands, the internal completion boundary, explicit positive-ID selectors for `schedule:add`, refusal of missing or conflicting selectors without prompting in every mode, output modes, and the Doctor family token, and generated context is current. Proof: `composer docs-lint`.

C9: CLI checks pass. Proof: `cd apps/cli && composer check`.

C10: Development verification uses focused affected Pest tests through TIA and changed-project checks. The finished exact candidate passes the Builder root `composer check` gate with TIA. Proof: affected Pest tests, `cd apps/cli && composer check`, and root `composer check`.

C11: `schedule:add --instance=INSTANCE --no-start` sends `start=false`, and `schedule:activate UUID` enables a previously installed AppInstance timer; human and JSON output show desired timer state separately from lifecycle state, while `schedule:run` remains one manual invocation. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.

C12: A production Schedule can be installed stopped, manually run without activating its timer, and explicitly activated after a first release; repeating activation preserves the same Schedule. Proof: Incus action `schedule-cli-production-activation`.

issue.title: Add Schedule and Doctor commands to the CLI
issue.description:
An operator manages Schedules for a Node or an AppInstance from the CLI with `schedule:add`, `schedule:list`, `schedule:show`, `schedule:run`, `schedule:logs`, `schedule:remove`, and `schedule:activate`, each an HTTP-only call through the PHP SDK, and `orbit doctor` renders the `schedule` family. `schedule:add` requires exactly one explicit `--node=ID` or `--instance=ID` selector with a positive integer ID; it never guesses or prompts for a target. Completion remains an internal Node-authenticated API and SDK transport outside the operator CLI. The operations are in [ADR 0013](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0013-native-systemd-schedule-management.md>) and the completion boundary is refined by [ADR 0060](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0060-record-latest-schedule-run-status.md>).

## Scope

* In: `schedule:add`, `schedule:list`, `schedule:show`, `schedule:run`, `schedule:logs`, `schedule:remove`, and `schedule:activate` over the PHP SDK; add selects exactly one Node or AppInstance target, list retains the existing unfiltered SDK operation, and the remaining commands use one Schedule UUID
* In: locally decidable option validation before HTTP, deterministic human and `--json` output, request IDs, safe shared errors, and bounded log rendering
* In: deterministic explicit target selection for `schedule:add`: exactly one positive-integer `--node=ID` or `--instance=ID`, with the same refusal behavior in interactive, non-interactive, and `--json` modes
* In: `schedule` as a `doctor --family` token
* In: the CLI command inventory, guidance, README, and generated context
* In: preserving the internal Node-authenticated completion API and SDK transport without exposing `CompleteScheduleRequest` through an operator command
* Out: Workspace targets
* Out: local SSH, systemd, `journalctl`, shell, curl, or Schedule execution on the operator machine
* Out: target lookup by name, implicit target discovery, and target-selection prompts in any mode
* Out: target, placement, authorization, and policy decisions, which stay in the Gateway
* Out: Gateway, PHP SDK, production deployment, and harness changes

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each of the seven operator commands sends exactly one SDK request for its operation and renders the typed response in human and `--json` form with the request ID, and a Gateway failure renders the shared safe error. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] `schedule:add` requires exactly one explicit `--node=ID` or `--instance=ID` with a positive integer ID. Both selectors, neither selector, a malformed or non-positive ID, or an option that belongs to the other target kind fails before any HTTP request. `--no-start` is AppInstance-only. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] `schedule:list` output contains no command text and `schedule:logs` renders only the bounded lines the Gateway returns. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] Interactive, non-interactive, and `--json` calls apply the same explicit-selector rules. Invalid target input returns a bounded error naming the required selector or invalid identity, never opens a target-selection prompt, and sends no discovery or operation request. `schedule:list` uses its existing unfiltered SDK operation; show, run, logs, remove, and activate identify one Schedule by UUID rather than by new target selectors. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] `orbit doctor --family=schedule` is accepted and renders the `schedule` family at its position in the ordered family set without asserting a numeric family count. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Doctor/DoctorCommandTest.php`.
- [ ] The command inventory and guidance list the seven operator commands, state that completion remains internal Node-authenticated API and SDK transport, and name no local host-execution dependency. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/BoostGuidanceTest.php`.
- [ ] From the operator machine, `schedule:add`, `schedule:show`, `schedule:run`, `schedule:logs`, and `schedule:remove` succeed against a real Node target and a real app-dev AppInstance target, and the logs output shows the run's journald lines. Proof: Incus action `schedule-cli-lifecycle`.
- [ ] Maintained documentation states the seven operator Schedule commands, the internal completion boundary, explicit positive-ID selectors for `schedule:add`, refusal of missing or conflicting selectors without prompting in every mode, output modes, and the Doctor family token, and generated context is current. Proof: `composer docs-lint`.
- [ ] CLI checks pass. Proof: `cd apps/cli && composer check`.
- [ ] Development verification uses focused affected Pest tests through TIA and changed-project checks. The finished exact candidate passes the Builder root `composer check` gate with TIA. Proof: affected Pest tests, `cd apps/cli && composer check`, and root `composer check`.
- [ ] `schedule:add --instance=INSTANCE --no-start` sends `start=false`, and `schedule:activate UUID` enables a previously installed AppInstance timer; human and JSON output show desired timer state separately from lifecycle state, while `schedule:run` remains one manual invocation. Proof: `apps/cli/tests/Feature/Schedules/ScheduleCommandsTest.php`.
- [ ] A production Schedule can be installed stopped, manually run without activating its timer, and explicitly activated after a first release; repeating activation preserves the same Schedule. Proof: Incus action `schedule-cli-production-activation`.

# ORB-71 replaced discovery attempt

Issue: ORB-71
Attempt: ccdd0df29280e73ea66bb45aac4e0813
Archived state: e2e-state.tar.gz
Archive SHA-256: 678602c044af57e9504c42711621907b7f0a1101c0de75ebfc76ff7ee852ffdc

The archive contains `.e2e/attempt.json`, `.e2e/topology.json`, and the complete `.e2e/log` through line 96.

## Retained acceptance observations

- Lines 74-78: Node 2 Schedule `42ad5b37-81e8-45c1-949a-ec6f59a2637d` completed add, show, run, 25-line logs, and remove with exit 0. Logs contained `orb71-node-run19-line`; removal reported `last_run_status=success`.
- Lines 79-83: app-dev AppInstance 1 Schedule `4f46e16f-6847-477e-8559-867c1867318b` completed add, show, run, 25-line logs, and remove with exit 0. Logs contained `orb71-dev-run19-line`; removal reported `last_run_status=success`.
- Lines 30-48: the earlier production Schedule `a748e4d3-9abd-4c40-89d3-01ba83c38c47` was installed stopped, deployed, manually invoked, activated twice with the same UUID, and removed. Before the ORB-304 prerequisite, service execution failed with `Permission denied` and systemd `203/EXEC`; the bounded Schedule logs carried that result.
- Lines 60-63: read-only metadata showed uutils coreutils `install` 0.8.0, `/etc/orbit` and `/etc/orbit/php-fpm` as real `0700 root:root` directories, `/etc/orbit/schedules` as a real `0755 root:root` directory, and no extended ACL grants.

## Replacement reason and setup observations

- Lines 65-69 synchronized the integrated source, corrected one migration-status working-directory mistake, confirmed all migrations ran, and verified the topology.
- Lines 84-86 found the expected untracked app-dev `composer.lock` and moved it to `/tmp/orb71-run19-composer.lock` for production clone setup.
- Line 87: supported clone to production AppInstance 3 failed at `production-source-prepare` because the disposable production home retained content from removed AppInstance 2, as required by ADR 0031.
- Lines 88-91 inspected the failed reserved record, retained production home, and source markers. Normal forced removal at line 90 was refused because the AppInstance was not active.
- Line 92: a second supported clone was refused because the failed reservation owned the App production placement.
- Lines 93-96: before the coordinator classified the retained content and authorized topology replacement, the implementer created `/tmp/orb71-run19-retained-home` and moved the retained `.env` and `releases` there. No `/etc/orbit` permission was changed and no clone retry followed. This raw disposable setup correction is preserved here and will disappear with topology release.

The coordinator authorized native release and fresh acquisition because the retained production content was expected product behavior but made this reused disposable topology unsuitable for a clean C12 rerun.
